# Step 2.246: the build's own checks do not depend on today's date (builder)

**The cause.** Not a fixed date: an hour. The made-up world already dates its games from its own clock (stand-in-world-seed.ts), and game 1 is "today at 18:00" in the league's zone (America/Chicago). `npm run test:web` started the world on the real clock, so every evening from 18:00 Chicago (00:00 UTC) to midnight there game 1 had started and, since step 2.159, rightly read "Awaiting score". `--now=2026-11-26T03:00:00Z` reproduces it on the old line.

**The fix (T-404, pending).** `scripts/check-web-shell.mjs` starts the server with `LOCAL_NOW` at noon in the league's zone on its today (`worldAtNoon`, as the browser tests do); `--now=<UTC time>` moves it. The clock helpers moved from `tests/browser/web-browser-kit.mjs` (which re-exports them) to `scripts/league-clock.mjs`, with one new one, `leagueDay(worldNow, days)`. The check's sentence and the product's rule are unchanged.

**Siblings found.**

- Fixed: check-web-shell's "mark as left" on 2026-11-13 and its "left on Fri, Nov 13" (now 12 days before the world's today); `rounds-test` (three Sundays in Jan 2027), `season-shown-test` (rounds on 2027-01-10/17), `reschedule-test` (new date 2027-03-06, "Mar 6"), `fixture-import-test` (a file of Jan 2027 games, 2027-02-30) now use days over a year after the world's today; `season-settings-test` types the live season's days as -85 and +17 days from today, as far from the world's games as 2026-09-01 and 2026-12-12 were when written.
- Left alone, they cannot flip: the seed's `left: '2026-10-02'` and `'2026-11-01'` (past, and those entries have no joined day); `signedInAt` 2026-11-01 in stand-in-ports.ts (already past); unit tests with fixed dates pass their own clock or `vi.setSystemTime` (team-pages, database-public-schedule, seed-demo-league, game-content's `startText`, which reads no clock); stand-in-admin-teams.test's leftOn 2026-11-13 (past, no joined day; its future case is next year from the clock).
- Not searched in full: `packages/database` store tests against the made-up database (they use its own `now()`), and the remaining browser tests beyond the grep for typed 2026/2027 dates.

**What ran.** `npm run test:web`: 288 checks passed at the default noon, and with `--no-build --now=` 2027-02-25T18:00Z (3 months on) and 2027-12-25T18:00Z (13 months on): 288 each. No tool in the repository moves the machine's own clock (only `vi.setSystemTime` in unit tests), so for the browser tests the reasoning is: every date they type is now a number of days from the world's today, so it stands as far from it on any day. Browser tests passed: game-states (164), first-test-walk (110), schedule-grid, season-shown (28), new-season (46), publish-preview (20); rounds (54), reschedule (15), fixture-import (24), season-settings (42). Also passed: `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, `npm test` (433 of 433, the T-404 pending file folds).

**Distrust.** Sessions keep the real clock while the world is at noon; nothing in the check compared them today, but a future check that does must pin both.
